_comment: Hardware-key triggers for Cybersyn's evdev layer (vendored from Key Mapper).
Deploy to ~/.termux/tasker/key_triggers.json on the phone.
Each entry fires an `external_trigger` event whose `trigger` is the entry's id --
the same event path the Quick Tap stub uses -- so an ordinary EVENT profile with
config {event: external_trigger, trigger: <id>} runs whatever task you want. No
task dispatch logic lives in the key layer.
Fields:
id       required, the trigger name matched by the profile
key      single key: VOLUME_UP | VOLUME_DOWN | POWER
keys     multiple keys, with mode PARALLEL (held together) or SEQUENCE (in order)
click    SHORT (default) | LONG | DOUBLE
mode     SINGLE (default) | PARALLEL | SEQUENCE
consume  true swallows the key so Android never sees it. Default false.
consume=true swallows EVERY press of that key while the trigger is registered --
a first press cannot know whether it will become a double press -- so the key's
normal function is gone. Prefer false unless you really mean to take the key over.
POWER is never consumable: long-press power stays native by design.
Changes are picked up on the next explicit reload:
am broadcast -a com.termux.cybersyn.action.RELOAD_PROFILES -p com.termux.cybersyn
(the -p is mandatory -- an implicit broadcast never reaches a manifest receiver)
or simply on the next start of the automation service.
Gyro/clutch and browser nav are NOT configured here: they are hold-to-act (they fire
on press and again on release), which a click-type model cannot express, so they
stay on the raw key path in KeyHijackController.
